note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 4(5), NAM 5; A06b Const 4(5), NAM 5; L05 Const 4(8)(a), NAM 7(1)(a)-(c)): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Parental residence restriction) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Namibian Constitution, Art. 4(1)(c)-(d), (2)(a), (5), as amended (NamibLII text, version of 13 October 2014); Namibian Citizenship Act 14 of 1990 (Government Gazette 65, 30 August 1990), ss. 5(1)(g), 7(1)(a), 26 (NamibLII text, version of 29 July 1994). It confirmed the years of residence, renunciation, loss on taking another citizenship, birth in the territory, birth in the territory's condition and descent. NamibLII is a legal information institute reproducing the Constitution and Government Gazette 65 of 30 August 1990, so its texts are secondary; they confirm every figure.

sources.said: Person has been lawfully and ordinarily resident for at least 10 years. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... Person is a naturalised citizen and voluntarily acquires another citizenship or acquires it involuntarily and fails to renounce the other citizenship within 1 year. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Namibia to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen and birth is registered with consular authorities. ... Parental residence restriction ... Person is born in Namibia to a person who is ordinarily resident at the time of birth. Other conditions: parents are not enjoying diplomatic immunity, nor represent another country, nor members of any police or military unit seconded for service in Namibia, nor illegal immigrants. ... sources.said: (c) those born in Namibia after the date of Independence whose fathers or mothers are Namibian citizens at the time of the birth of such persons; (d) those born in Namibia after the date of Independence who do not qualify for citizenship under Sub-Article (c) hereof, and whose fathers or mothers are ordinarily resident in Namibia at the time of the birth of such persons: provided that their fathers or mothers are not then persons: (aa) enjoying diplomatic immunity in Namibia under any law relating to diplomatic privileges; or (bb) who are career representatives of another country; or (cc) who are members of any police, military or security unit seconded for service within Namibia by the Government of another country; or (dd) who are illegal immigrants ... (5) Citizenship by naturalisation may be applied for by persons who are not Namibian citizens under Sub-Articles (1), (2), (3) or (4) hereof and who: (a) are ordinarily resident in Namibia at the time when the application for naturalisation is made; and (b) have been so resident in Namibia for a continuous period of not less than ten (10) years;

sources.said: (g) he or she is willing to renounce the citizenship of any foreign country of which he or she is a citizen ... 7. Loss of Namibian citizenship acquired by registration or naturalisation (1) A Namibian citizen who has acquired his or her citizenship by registration or naturalisation shall cease to be a Namibian citizen as such if, on or after the date of Independence - (a) such person is of or over the age of 18 years, and by voluntary act other than marriage acquires the citizenship of a foreign country ... 26. Prohibition of dual citizenship Subject to the provisions of this Act or any other law, no Namibian citizen shall also be a citizen of a foreign country.
